newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Prices steady with two deals done.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Prices steady with two deals done.

text.p: Singapore high sulphur fuel oil prices stayed at around their recent levels on Tuesday with two cargoes exchanging hands, traders said.
Late on Tuesday, a 380-cst cargo was traded at $95 per tonne, slightly firmer than Monday's $94.5 traded level.
The 180-cst grade was traded at $98 per tonne, unchanged from Monday's level.
Three majors had been offering cargoes in the past few weeks and buyers were mainly a Singapore-based trading firm and a bunker supplier from the Middle East, traders said.
Some traders saw more than enough supplies while some said demand and supply were balanced at present.
"The Singapore trader is still buying recently, which supports the market, but he will stop if the 180-cst grade hits $100 per tonne," said one trader.
Another trader said some majors were offering cargoes regularly possibly because they to have no requirements in the near term.
Fuel oil swaps were stable, with August last quoted at $98.50/$99.00 and September at $98.50/$99.50.
The market is waiting for results of a Taiwan tender to buy low sulphur fuel oil, traders said.
Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) is expected to announce late on Wednesday results of a tender to buy 0.5-percent sulphur fuel oil for September delivery.
The tender is seeking a 38,000-tonne low-pour cargo for September 1-15 and a high-pour cargo for September 11-30.
